name: Engineering Tracked Delivery
description: A change checked against the original request, with test results, independent review and a recorded release status. The record shows what was completed and what still needs attention.
audience: Product and engineering teams delivering repository changes
problem: Engineering requests fail when requirements, dependencies, verification, and review live only in chat or are compressed into implementation.
outcome: A change checked against the original request, with test results, independent review and a recorded release status. The record shows what was completed and what still needs attention.
whyAi: AI can coordinate discovery, implementation, testing, and review across a long-running change while StackOS preserves dependencies and proof.
operatorPath: Describe the desired outcome, constraints, and authority boundary.
Review material design choices or production-risk gates.
Inspect verification, review findings, and residual risk before release.
agentPath: Clarify the request, affected users and systems, constraints, and what will count as a successful result.
Inspect the existing code, choose an approach and checks, then plan tasks in dependency order. Review the plan before implementation.
Implement authorized tasks, running independent work in parallel when useful. Test and independently review each result before starting dependent work, then check that the pieces work together.
Compare the finished change with the original request, record test and review results, and state whether it was released or what remains. Close the work only when the evidence supports that status.
progressSignals: Ticket delivery and review in progress
recovery: Record blockers in the run and tracker instead of hiding them in chat.
Use run consistency and recovery operations to resume a blocked step without losing prior handoffs.
Before reopening an earlier gate, stop active assignments and their processes, preserve evidence, and reconcile affected child tickets explicitly. Existing runs retain their frozen step order.
safeStoppingPoints: Stop after a reviewed design or diagnosis when implementation authority was not granted.
prerequisites: A desired outcome and acceptance boundary
Authority for the requested file or system changes
whenToUse: A user asks for engineering work that needs planning, implementation, review, and signoff.
A user explicitly asks to use a workflow, engineering workflow, StackOS workflow, "the workflow", or to follow the SDLC for engineering delivery.
A user asks for release-grade delivery or equivalent lifecycle language that implies requirements-to-release enforcement.
Work should be visible as tracker tasks/tickets with dependencies, blockers, evidence, and release state.
A project wants host-local agents configured from SDLC presets for a concrete delivery flow.
The change touches contracts, tests, UI, data, provider behavior, MCP/REST/CLI operation surfaces, docs, or release risk.

stages.title: Scope Work
stages.summary: Restate the engineering goal, delivery mode, constraints, project setup, host-agent format, and missing context.

stages.title: Define Requirements And Flows
stages.summary: Convert user intent into explicit user, data, system, and business flows, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and evidence expectations.

stages.title: Discover Impact
stages.summary: Map affected scopes, real execution paths, ownership boundaries, downstream readers, tests, docs, and signoff fallout.

stages.title: Design Approach
stages.summary: Identify canonical ownership, shared operations, data invariants, adapter surfaces, grants, docs, tests, rollout, and rollback implications.

stages.title: Design Tests, TDD, And Manual Scenarios
stages.summary: Own the full proof plan before delivery: TDD/red-first automated tests, verification commands, agent-executed E2E/manual flow scenarios, expected…

stages.title: Plan Tracker Tickets
stages.summary: Turn the completed design and proof plan into executable assignments with dependencies, exclusive ownership, acceptance criteria, review instructions,…

stages.title: Delivery Readiness Review
stages.summary: Review the complete requirements, design, proof plan, executable tickets, dependencies, and resources before implementation.

stages.title: Deliver Tickets
stages.summary: Delegate ready tickets, independently verify each candidate immediately, and accept integrated results before completing tickets and releasing dependents.

stages.title: Verify Delivery
stages.summary: Prove the assembled outcome, cross-ticket interactions, remaining requirements, and mandatory project checks using current ticket receipts plus the…

stages.title: Review Delivery
stages.summary: Independently review the assembled outcome and remaining integration risks across behavior, contracts, security, docs, evidence, and release authority.

stages.title: Audit Tracker Truth
stages.summary: Confirm tracker state, run-plan state, docs, tests, evidence, and the actual diff agree before closeout.

stages.title: Release Closeout
stages.summary: Confirm final signoff, docs, known limitations, commit/release state, rollback/watch notes, and post-release checks.
